34. is to be praised,
because in him was the multitude of wisdom.
And on the other side of the tomb was written:
"You, O earth,
although you cover the body of Plato,
to his soul, however, you do not draw near at all,
because it does not die."
And Aristotle was the son of Nicomachus the physician, from the village of Tagira (Stagira?) in the country of Macedonia.
And on both father's and mother's side his descent traces back to Asclepiades.
And for a period of twenty years he was a hearer of Plato.
And when he was not present for some time with the rest of the disciples,
Plato would say to those who were present:
"The mind has not come;
far is the philosopher from the truth,
dumb are his hearers."
And Aristotle had great honor with kings,
and by his guidance Alexander directed the affairs of his kingdom.
And when he went to war against the kings of the earth,
Aristotle was left free {OCR?},
and began to write books on logic, natural sciences, theology, and ethics.
He was handsome in stature,
and fair-complexioned,
with small eyes and mouth,
a broad chest,
a thick beard,
and a flat nose.
And his eyes were piercing.
And he was hasty in his pace when he walked alone,
but with others he walked deliberately.
And from reading books, often times sleep would abandon him.
And he would pause over every word,
and reflect upon its force.
And when he was asked,
he would not answer quickly,
but after some time.
And he loved music.
And when anyone disputed with him,
he was not at all concerned about that man's victory,
but about the truth.
And if he erred,
he would admit it.
And whenever the truth was with his companion,
he would acknowledge it.
Now, his clothing, his food, his drink, his marriage, and his movements were moderate.
And he died at the age of sixty-eight years,
and left behind a son, a daughter, a wife, male and female slaves, and much property.
And Theophrastus his nephew succeeded him in teaching.
And when he was dying, he made an excellent will regarding the affairs of his household and his disciples.
